title: Bloom filter
summary: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic data structure for set membership testing. Structure: bit array of m bits, k hash functions. Insert: set bits at positions h_1(x), h_2(x), ..., h_k(x). Query: check if all k bits are 1. False positives possible; false negatives impossible. False positive rate ≈ (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k. Optimal k = (m/n) * ln(2).

structure.meaning: k independent hash functions, each mapping to [0, m-1].
Set bits at h_1(x), h_2(x), ..., h_k(x) to 1.
Check if all bits at h_1(x), ..., h_k(x) are 1. If yes, probably in set. If any is 0, definitely not in set.
P ≈ (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k. With optimal k = (m/n)ln(2), P ≈ 0.6185^(m/n).
Uses counters instead of bits. Supports deletion (decrement counters).
Uses cuckoo hashing. Supports deletion and has better cache locality.

notes: Bloom filters are used in databases (LSM trees), caches, network routers, and spell checkers.
Bloom filters trade space for accuracy (false positives, no false negatives).
Cuckoo filters are an alternative with deletion support and better locality.
Bloom filters are used by Cassandra, HBase, Chrome (Safe Browsing), and many others.
Counting Bloom filters support deletion by using counters instead of bits.
